title: Ilkhanate
summary: The Ilkhanate was the Mongol realm founded by the Mongol general Hulegu, centred on Iran and Iraq. In 1256 his armies took the Ismaili fortresses, ending with Alamut, and on 13 February 1258 they captured Baghdad, sacked it for a week and executed the last Abbasid caliph. The Ilkhans ruled from Azerbaijan, with Tabriz as capital, and Hulegu built Nasir al-Din Tusi an observatory at Maragha. Ghazan converted to Islam in 1295, and the realm broke apart after Abu Said's death in 1335.

uncertainty.note: Hulagu subdued Persian strongholds in 1256 and took Baghdad in 1258; the state broke up following the death of Abu Sa'id in 1335, with petty claimant dynasties lingering until 1353.

where.modern_name: Tabriz, East Azerbaijan, Iran (capital of the Ilkhanate; the realm encompassed modern Iran, Iraq, Azerbaijan, Armenia, and parts of Turkey, Syria, and Afghanistan)
where.historical_name: Tabriz, capital of the Ilkhanate (Mongol Ulus of Hulagu)

importance.justification: Mongol rule over Iran and Iraq that ended the Abbasid caliphate and joined Persia to Mongol Eurasia (R3 D3 T3 L3).

audience_note: Mentions the sack of Baghdad and the killing of its people.
reviewer_note: Coordinator review 2026-11-13: missing link 1206-mongol-empire replaced with 1206-founding-of-the-mongol-empire; Baghdad siege linked. Summary rewritten from Encyclopaedia Iranica and WHE. Start 1256 (Iranica: campaign against the Ismailis); WHE dates the state 1260-1335.
